fixes.explanation: That's it, friend. The disciples rebuked those who brought the children. The people brought them so Jesus could place His hands on them, and a rebuke is what they got. I think those folks were not expecting that at all.

I'd love to tell you the disciples set up a nice orderly line, but that's not what happened. The text says the disciples rebuked those who brought the children. No line shows up in the text, just a rebuke. I think a line would have been a much better plan.
Nope, the text doesn't show the disciples carrying anyone. People were bringing the children, and the disciples rebuked those who brought them. So the answer is the rebuke, friend.

Right on the money, baker. Jesus says, “For the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.” That's the reason He gives for not hindering the little children. The disciples had rebuked those who brought them, and Jesus tells them not to hinder them.

I can see why you'd think that, friend, because rule-keeping sounds impressive. But that's not what Jesus says here. He says the kingdom of God belongs to such as these, right in the middle of talking about the little children.

Teachers of the law don't come up in this scene, baker. Jesus says, “For the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.” He says it about the little children the people brought, after the disciples rebuked those people.
Yes, this one is False. Jesus says, “Truly I tell you, anyone who does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it.” Never, friend. That's how plainly He puts it.

True, and what a scene. After all those words, Jesus took the children in His arms, placed His hands on them, and blessed them. The people had brought the children for Him to place His hands on them, and He did that and blessed them too.

That's the one, baker. The man ran up, knelt, and asked, “Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?” I think he was serious about it. A man who runs up and kneels doesn't look like he's asking a small question to me.
Good guess, but the man doesn't ask about the commandments. Jesus brings them up after the man's question. The man asks what he must do to inherit eternal life.

Temple? Friend, the temple isn't anywhere in this verse. Jesus says to go, sell everything he owns, and give to the poor. Then the man will have treasure in heaven, and after that he's invited to come follow Jesus.

Hold on, friend, priests aren't mentioned in this verse. Jesus says the man should sell everything he owns and give to the poor. Heaven is where the treasure is, and then he's invited to follow Jesus.
Yes, and it's a heavy moment. The text says the man was saddened by these words and went away in sorrow. Jesus had just invited him to come follow Him. I think this one hurts.
True, friend. The text says the disciples were amazed at His words. Jesus had just said, “How hard it is for the rich to enter the kingdom of God!” I bet that one landed hard.
Right, baker. Jesus says, “But many who are first will be last, and the last will be first.” Notice the word many. That flips how people usually think about who's in front.
Tests don't show up in this verse, baker. Jesus says, “But many who are first will be last, and the last will be first.” Many who are first will be last, and the last will be first.
